subject: ventures/obsidian-plugin-review-check
professional: an Obsidian community-plugin reviewer (obsidianmd/obsidian-releases and the community.obsidian.md automated review) who first checks manifest.json against docs.obsidian.md/Reference/Manifest (required fields incl. isDesktopOnly, id/name forbidden words, x.y.z version), leftover sample-plugin content, and the Plugin guidelines' Security section (innerHTML/outerHTML/insertAdjacentHTML), the same ground eslint-plugin-obsidianmd's validate-manifest, sample-names and prefer-create-el rules cover

evidence.correctness: Recomputed against sources the author did not write: the real template (git clone obsidianmd/obsidian-sample-plugin, master f8667ce 2026-04-24), docs.obsidian.md Manifest.md, Plugin guidelines.md and Submit your plugin.md (raw from obsidianmd/obsidian-developer-docs main), and eslint-plugin-obsidianmd docs/rules/validate-manifest.md. (1) The template's author has been "Obsidian" since 2020-10-28 (`git log -p -- manifest.json`; before that "Licat"), never "Your Name", so the author placeholder check can never fire on a real template; on the real template the tool flags id and name only and misses author "Obsidian" and the template description. (2) Manifest.md marks isDesktopOnly **Required: Yes**; the tool reports it as optional and exits 0 without it. (3) Constructed manifest {id:'my-obsidian-plugin', name:'Obsidian Plugin Helper', version:'v1.0', description:'this plugin does stuff', author:'Obsidian'} breaks five documented rules (id contains obsidian and ends with plugin; name contains Obsidian and Plugin; version not x.y.z; isDesktopOnly missing; description format per validate-manifest): `cd /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-oss-monorepo/f59c5cce-fbdc-5341-97d2-6a5629e767ca/scratchpad/obsidian && node /home/user/oss-monorepo/ventures/obsidian-plugin-review-check/check.mjs fx/a` -> all [OK], exit 0. (4) innerHTML detector on 6 hand-written lines: misses `el.innerHTML += userInput`, `const u = "https://example.com"; el.innerHTML = u;` (the `//` comment strip runs before string stripping and truncates the line), a two-line assignment and `el["innerHTML"] =`, and flags only `/* el.innerHTML = commented */`, a false positive the stripper's own doc comment says it handles: observed unsafe lines [6], expected [1,2,3,5]. (5) versions.json: sample README says it exists 'so older versions of Obsidian can download an older version'; a plugin whose current minAppVersion equals the previous entry's is not blocked, yet `cd /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-oss-monorepo/f59c5cce-fbdc-5341-97d2-6a5629e767ca/scratchpad/obsidian && node /home/user/oss-monorepo/ventures/obsidian-plugin-review-check/check.mjs fx/c` exits 1 and calls it release-blocking; with no versions.json at all (Submit your plugin lists only README, LICENSE, manifest.json) it prints '[?] not checked' and still exits 1. Simple positive cases (plain innerHTML=, insertAdjacentHTML(, console.log, sample id/name) are right.
evidence.completeness: Each README/index feature run: required-field check (works for its 6 fields), placeholder check (id/name work, author can never match the real template), versions.json cross-check (works as specified), innerHTML/outerHTML/insertAdjacentHTML (simple forms only), addEventListener and console.log notes (work), CLI --json and exit codes (work), browser folder picker and worked example (code read, shares scan.mjs; not clicked in a browser). Additional-manifest note works but the wrong manifest is chosen (see craft). The block-comment stripping promised in scan.mjs's stripCommentsAndStrings doc comment is not implemented. No stubs or TODOs; served page https://marisstella.app/obsidian-plugin-review-check/ returns 200.
evidence.verification: `cd ventures/obsidian-plugin-review-check && node --test '*.test.mjs'` -> 63 pass, 0 fail. 5 mutants via quality_mutate.py: dropping outerHTML from the assignment regex caught; dropping the placeholder gate from ok caught; changing the author placeholder caught (the test pins the author's wrong value); deleting double-quote string stripping SURVIVED; widening CONSOLE_LOG to console.warn SURVIVED. Tests assert the author's beliefs ('Your Name', isDesktopOnly optional) rather than the template or the docs.
evidence.craft: Read scan.mjs, check.mjs, index.html script, check.test.mjs, page.test.mjs. Small and readable, one shared scan.mjs for CLI and browser. Defects: check.mjs:106 takes the first manifest.json in walk order, so a subfolder fixture (aaa-test/manifest.json) is read and the root manifest is reported as 'additional ... not read' (`{C} fx/e`); scan.mjs:138 strips `//` before strings, so any URL string hides the rest of the line; no `/* */` stripping; the root main.js build bundle is scanned as source (`{C} fx/d` flags main.js:2), unlike eslint-plugin-obsidianmd's documented globalIgnores; index.html:240 writes manifest-derived text through td.innerHTML, the very pattern the tool flags; browser skip list (index.html:124) differs from the CLI's (all dot-dirs).
evidence.claims: Disclaimer, no-warranty, non-affiliation and 'not a determination' text present on every page. Unbacked or false: 'the official obsidian-sample-plugin template ships ... author "Your Name"' (README.md:18, index.html:46 and :306, VENTURE.yaml:9) contradicted by the template's git history; 'one of the easiest release-blocking mistakes' (README.md:14, versions-json-missing-entry.html:36, check.mjs:165) contradicted by the sample README's stated purpose of versions.json; vs-guessing page: 'this tool's field list is checked against Obsidian's published guidelines' and 'both it and Obsidian's docs agree' (false: isDesktopOnly), 'runs the same field, placeholder, and API checks a reviewer would', and 'Obsidian's own developer documentation ... explains that versions.json needs its own matching entry for the current version' (not in Manifest.md, Submit your plugin.md or Plugin guidelines.md); vs-eslint page says 'five-check' / 'covers five things' and lists four; llms.txt:5 says 'Results are estimates from the numbers typed in' for a file scanner. Served llms.txt hosts are correct (served-copy.mjs: no placeholder origin).
evidence.fitness: Job walked: a developer runs the checker before submitting. On the real sample template it correctly flags id/name and console.log. On fixture a, a manifest the automated review and validate-manifest reject on five counts, it reports clean and exits 0; on fixture c, a valid plugin without versions.json, it exits 1. A reviewer would get more from eslint-plugin-obsidianmd's validate-manifest (all 7 required fields, name/description word and format checks) plus its prefer-create-el rule; the tool's one unique check (versions.json entry) guards a non-blocking condition. Also the current Submit your plugin doc routes submissions through community.obsidian.md, while the pages describe only obsidian-releases PR comments.
evidence.domain: Compared to docs.obsidian.md Manifest reference, Plugin guidelines (Security, Resource management, console logging), Submit your plugin, the obsidian-sample-plugin repo and eslint-plugin-obsidianmd validate-manifest. Departures: isDesktopOnly treated as optional; no id rules (lowercase/hyphens, no 'obsidian', not ending 'plugin'), no name rules (no Obsidian/Plugin), no x.y.z version check, no description format check, wrong author placeholder and no description placeholder; versions.json semantics overstated into a release gate; innerHTML heuristic misses `+=`, the most common append form. The innerHTML/outerHTML/insertAdjacentHTML guidance itself is correctly cited, and the addEventListener note matches the Resource management section.

defects.what: Sample-plugin author placeholder is "Your Name", a value the official template has never shipped (author has been "Obsidian" since 2020-10-28); the check cannot fire on a real template and the real leftover (author "Obsidian", template description) passes. Stated as fact on README, index.html, VENTURE.yaml.
isDesktopOnly is required per docs.obsidian.md Manifest reference (and validate-manifest), but is reported as optional and never fails the check; a manifest missing it exits 0.

A manifest breaking five documented rules (id contains 'obsidian' and ends 'plugin', name contains Obsidian/Plugin, version 'v1.0' not x.y.z, no isDesktopOnly, self-referential description) reports clean and exits 0 as a CI gate.

innerHTML heuristic misses `el.innerHTML += x` (regex requires = right after optional whitespace), and any line where a string containing '//' (a URL) precedes the assignment, because the line-comment strip runs before string stripping.
Block comments are not stripped although the doc comment says they are: `/* el.innerHTML = x */` is flagged as a failing finding.

A missing current-version entry in versions.json, or no versions.json at all, fails the check and is called 'release-blocking'; per the sample plugin README versions.json is the fallback map for older app versions, and Submit your plugin does not require it.

'one of the easiest release-blocking mistakes' and 'Obsidian's own developer documentation ... explains that versions.json needs its own matching entry for the current version' are not backed by any Obsidian doc.
'this tool's field list is checked against Obsidian's published guidelines' / 'runs the same field, placeholder, and API checks a reviewer would' are false (isDesktopOnly, id/name/version rules).
First manifest.json in walk order wins, so a subfolder manifest (test fixture, example vault) is checked and the root plugin manifest is ignored; browser uses the first in file order the same way.
The built main.js bundle in the plugin root is scanned as source, so bundled-library innerHTML fails the check after any local build.
'five-check pre-flight pass' / 'covers five things' then lists four.
llms.txt boilerplate 'Results are estimates from the numbers typed in' does not describe a file scanner.
The results table writes manifest-derived text (version, field names) through td.innerHTML, the pattern the tool itself flags; self-XSS only, but a reviewer would note it.
Pages describe review only as obsidian-releases PR comments; the current Submit your plugin doc routes submissions through community.obsidian.md with an automated review.
Two seeded mutants survive (removing double-quote string stripping; widening console.log match): no test covers string stripping or the console pattern's boundaries.

verdict: Does not meet the bar. The code is small, tidy and its 63 tests pass, but checked against the real obsidian-sample-plugin repository and docs.obsidian.md, its domain facts are wrong where it matters: the 'Your Name' author placeholder has never been in the template, isDesktopOnly is required but treated as optional, none of the documented id/name/version/description rules are checked (a manifest breaking five of them exits 0), the innerHTML heuristic misses `+=` and any line after a URL string, and its one check eslint-plugin-obsidianmd lacks (versions.json entry) guards a condition the docs do not treat as blocking while failing plugins that have no versions.json. Pages repeat the wrong facts as Obsidian's. Disclaimers and served URLs are fine.
